chunks: Whoever wants to do ghusl from janaba should strive to urinate first, so that whatever remains of semen in his urethra exits. Then he washes his hands three times before inserting them into the vessel. Then he does istinja and cleanses his private parts.

Then he places three handfuls of water on his head, separating the hair with his fingertips until the water reaches the root of all his hair. Then he takes the vessel in his hand and pours it over his head and body twice, passing his hand over all his body, and running his fingers through his ears. Everything the water touches is purified.
When the junub immerses himself in water with a single complete immersion, that suffices him for his ghusl. If he stands in the rain until it washes him, that also suffices for his ghusl.

Whoever wishes to rinse his mouth and nose during the ghusl of janaba may do so, but it is not obligatory, because ghusl applies to what is external, not to what is internal — except that if he wishes to eat or drink before ghusl, it is not permissible for him unless he first washes his hands and rinses his mouth and nose, for al-baras (a skin disease) is feared for him if he eats or drinks before that.
When the junub sweats in his garment and the janaba was from lawful intercourse, then prayer in that garment is lawful. But if it was from unlawful intercourse, then prayer in it is unlawful.

key_terms.الإحليل: The urethra; specifically here, the opening from which urine and semen exit
key_terms.الارتماس: Complete immersion in water as an alternative method for ghusl
key_terms.الاستنجاء: Istinja: ritual cleansing of the private parts after using the restroom
key_terms.البرص: Al-baras: a skin disease (traditionally translated as leprosy or vitiligo), feared as a consequence of eating/drinking before ghusl without rinsing
key_terms.الجنابة: Janaba: major ritual impurity, typically resulting from sexual intercourse or seminal emission
key_terms.الغسل: Ghusl: the full-body ritual bath required to lift major impurity
key_terms.المضمضة والاستنشاق: Rinsing the mouth and nose — recommended but not obligatory in ghusl

ai.seo_question: What is the correct way to perform ghusl from janaba according to Islamic law?
ai.summary: This legal ruling from Al-Amali of Sheikh Saduq provides a comprehensive and detailed description of the ghusl of janaba (the ritual bath following major ritual impurity). It covers the sequence of steps including urination, washing hands, istinja, pouring water over the head and body, and special cases such as complete immersion and standing under rain. The text also addresses the rulings on mouth and nose rinsing (recommended but not obligatory), eating/drinking before ghusl (requires preliminary washing), and how the lawfulness of the act that caused janaba affects prayer in the garment worn while sweating.
word_analysis: then let him strive/make an effort

en.bilal-muhammad: Someone who wants to do ghusl from janaba is to make an effort to urinate so that whatever is left in his urethra of semen exits out. Then, he washes his hands thrice before entering them into the vessel. Then, he does istinja and cleanses his private.

Then, he puts three handfuls of water on his head, and separates his hair with his fingertips until the water reaches the root of all of his hair. Then, he takes the vessels with his hand and pours it on his head and his body twice, and passes his hand on all of his body, and runs his finger through his ears. All that the water comes in contact with is thus purified.
When the junub immerses [himself] in water with a single (complete) immersion, that suffices him for his ghusl. When he stands in the rain until it washes him, that suffices him for his ghusl.

Whoever likes to do the mouth-rinsing and to do the nose-rinsing in the ghusl of janaba then he is to do so, but that is not obligatory as the ghusl is upon what is on the outside, not upon what is on the inside, except that when he wants to eat or drink prior to the ghusl it is not permissible for him unless he washes his hands and rinses his mouth and nose, for al-baras is feared for him if he eats or drinks prior to that.
When the junub sweats in his garment, and the janaba from a halal [intercourse], then prayer is halal in the garment. However, if it was from a haram [intercourse], then prayer is haram in it.
